data.description:
HAZARD. `hermes sessions export --format trace` (v0.18.2, upstream daedf4f6) emits Claude Code-shaped JSONL. toolbench's TB-13 schema dispatch detects the claude schema by `"sessionId" in entry` (parsers.py:83). Hermes trace records carry `sessionId`. Therefore hermes trace exports dropped into the corpus parse CLEANLY as ClaudeParser, yield real ToolCall rows, and raise no error -- while silently carrying `usage=None` on every call.

This is not TB-12's silent zero (calls dropped). It is the inverse: calls are KEPT, and the usage channel is silently null.

EVIDENCE. Exported 47 live sessions (`--min-tool-calls 3 --newer-than 2d`) to scratch, 650 records total:

  lines with message.usage : 0   (0.0%)
  lines with requestId     : 0   (0.0%)
  tool_use blocks          : 280

Ran the real detector and parser against one trace file (20260709_122716_09e9bb):

  detect_parser(...)  -> ClaudeParser        # not an error, not a skip
  parser.parse(...)   -> 13 tool calls, 0 malformed
  first call: name='skill_view' input_chars=24 output_chars=53679
              usage=None  duration_ms=None  no_result=False
              model='zai/GLM-5.1:US'  result_source='block_local'

Record envelope is genuinely Claude-shaped: parentUuid, isSidechain, sessionId, uuid, cwd, gitBranch, version, userType, timestamp, type. Only `message.usage` and `requestId` are absent.

BLAST RADIUS (narrow, but real -- verified, not assumed):

1. Cache-hit false negatives. `_is_cache_hit(usage)` (passive.py:174) returns False on `not usage`. Every hermes-trace call is therefore silently counted as a cache MISS. S19 says this signal is caveat-only and never used for ranking, which caps the damage -- but the denominator is still quietly contaminated.

2. requestId absent -> TB-16 arm isolability is IMPOSSIBLE on trace exports. TB-16 established that batches must be grouped by requestId, not timestamp. Trace exports carry neither. Any probe run over trace data silently regresses to the pre-TB-16 defect.

3. `tokens` is NOT poisoned. `ToolCall.tokens` = `output_chars // 4` (transcript.py:62), a char proxy independent of `usage`. The token leaderboard does not dilute. This is the one thing that survives.

NON-FINDING (do not "fix"). Payload-based dispatch classifying hermes traces as `claude` is CORRECT by design -- ClaudeParser's own docstring says "detection is by payload, not by producer: one parser, two agents". Schema and agent are separate axes. The bug is not the dispatch; it is that nothing marks the resulting rows as usage-less.

DO NOT MIGRATE hermes.py TO TRACE. toolbench/hermes.py already sets `usage=None` deliberately, with a documented honesty rationale (hermes.py:116): hermes records `token_count` per MESSAGE, not per tool call. The SQLite adapter therefore has strictly MORE information than the trace export (message-level token_count exists in the DB; trace drops it entirely). Trace is a viewer/sharing format, not a measurement format. Migrating would lose data and gain nothing.

SPEC SHEET CORRECTIONS (the pasted summary overstates):
  - "Six formats" is FIVE: `--format {jsonl,md,qmd,html,trace}`. PROMPTS is not a format; it is `--only {user-prompts}`, a filter flag layered on jsonl/md.
  - "+15 more" filters undercounts; there are 23 filter flags.
  - Confirmed accurate: shared filter engine w/ prune+archive (both subcommands exist); trace redacts by default (`--no-redact` is opt-out, trace-only); `--lineage {single,logical}`; `--delete-after-verified`; `--upload` to HF.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not chosen):
  a. Give ParseResult/ToolCall an explicit `usage_available: bool` (or make `usage` a tri-state) so a usage-less corpus is loud rather than null-by-omission. Cheapest, matches the "skip loudly" precedent from TB-13.
  b. Have detect_parser emit a provenance warning when a claude-schema file has 0/N `message.usage` across the detect window. Detects the hazard at ingest, not at report time.
  c. Refuse trace-shaped input in probe.py specifically (requestId is mandatory there), while allowing it in passive.py.
  d. Do nothing; document that trace exports are passive-only input.

ACCEPTANCE. Either (i) a usage-less transcript is structurally distinguishable from a usage-bearing one at parse time -- so `_is_cache_hit` cannot silently fabricate misses and probe.py cannot silently regress past TB-16 -- or (ii) SPEC.md states that `--format trace` output is out-of-corpus and the loader rejects it. A hermes trace export must not be able to enter the corpus and quietly report 280 tool calls whose cache-hit rate is a fiction.
data.title: hermes --format trace parses as claude but carries no usage or requestId; cache-hit signal silently fabricated

  cache_read_tokens>0 : 705
  tool_call_count > 0 : 724
  estimated_cost_usd>0: 199

The `sessions` table carries input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens, api_call_count, estimated_cost_usd, actual_cost_usd, cost_source, pricing_version. The correct rationale is: hermes records tokens at SESSION grain only; there is no per-message or per-tool-call token record to attribute. The conclusion (`usage=None`) is right; the stated reason is wrong and should be fixed so a future reader does not go looking for message-level tokens that were never there.

OPPORTUNITY (out of scope here, may deserve its own ticket). Session-grain `cache_read_tokens` (705/779 populated) is a real cache signal that toolbench currently ignores for hermes -- `_is_cache_hit` only ever consults per-call `usage`. hermes sessions are thus reported as 100% cache-miss today, from the SQLite path as well as the trace path.

data.body: CORRECTION TRAIL (first draft of this ticket was wrong). Initial version claimed the SQLite adapter beats trace because 'message-level token_count exists in the DB.' That was sourced from toolbench/hermes.py's own docstring, not from the database. Verifying against ~/.hermes/state.db read-only showed messages.token_count is NULL in 6672/6672 rows and is never written by any upstream code path. The DO-NOT-MIGRATE conclusion survives, on stronger and different grounds: sessions.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write,reasoning}_tokens + estimated/actual_cost_usd are populated in 734/779 sessions, and trace drops all of them. Lesson mirrors TB-13 correction #8: do not cite our own docstrings as evidence about someone else's data.

data.body:
Tasks 0-2 landed; stopping before passive.py per operator checkpoint.

VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA (not fixtures):
  - 64 real trace files (hermes v0.18.2): 64/64 -> HermesTraceParser, 369 calls all ABSENT_BY_EXPORT, 0 malformed
  - same run reproduces the hazard: 0/848 records carry message.usage or requestId
  - 300 real claude transcripts: 300/300 -> ClaudeParser, no AmbiguousSchema
  - 0 of 4,061 local transcripts carry a top-level version of 'hermes-agent'

PLAN DEFECTS FOUND BY EXECUTION (Task 0):
  1. The fix's health probe was 'SELECT 1' -- a constant expression that reads no page. It returns ok on the very database it must detect as unreadable, so the immutable=1 fallback would never have fired and the suite would have gone green with the bug intact. Now 'SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master'.
  2. The fixture assumed a clean close removes -wal/-shm. It does not (sqlite 3.43.2). The sidecar-less state must be produced by unlinking them.
  3. mode=ro fails ONLY when -wal is absent. A present -wal (empty or frame-bearing) reads fine, so the plan's 'pending frames' test could never pass. The -wal guard is a defensive invariant, now exercised by fault injection.
  4. The failing live test called sqlite3.connect directly, so no _connect change could ever have fixed it.

Also: the usage docstring was corrected against a fresh measurement -- messages.token_count is NULL on 10,177 rows across all four DBs (not 10,133; aphrodite-mood's 2,006 messages were unreadable until Task 0 landed).

REMAINING: Task 3 (passive counters + four-case render), Task 4 (probe fixture migration), Task 5 (probe.py NonIsolableTurns), Task 6 (docs). S30 is untouched: probe.py still has its timestamp fallback, so trace input can still silently regress it.

RUN-2 INTAKE (orchestrator): Tasks 0-2 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-09-tb-18-usage-provenance.md are COMMITTED AND PUSHED on chore/add-hermes-cli-export-plan (PR #20, OPEN). Remaining scope for the run-2 delegator: Tasks 3-6 ONLY, continuing that same branch — do not rebranch, do not redo Tasks 0-2. Task 4 (probe fixture requestId migration) MUST land before Task 5 deletes the ts: fallback. Task 6 (DOCS) has a SHARED-FILE overlap with TB-19 on README/EVALUATION — coordinate in the PR body. Verify counts against uv run pytest -q, never unittest discover.

Plan revalidated before Tasks 3-6 (commit 4cfd5d1). Mechanical drift only, no amendments to architecture: (1) SPEC.md/EVALUATION.md S29/S30 already landed during Phase 0 intake (305d7d8) -- Task 6 Step 1 is now a no-op, skipping it. (2) Test baseline is 232 passed/1 skipped (not 231 passed) due to the hermetic-suite fix (5baeca1) -- Tasks 3-6 will report actual gate counts rather than the plan's stated cumulative figures. (3) Task 6 Step 3's ticket-correction comment confirmed not yet posted; proceeding as written. Working against origin/main @ 28b6187. Proceeding to implement Tasks 3-6.

Correction to the ticket body: '--format trace: tokens is NOT poisoned' overstates the evidence. Measured redacted vs --no-redact across 43 sessions / 270 calls: output_chars delta 12 => 3 tokens (~0.004%). Negligible but nonzero. The usage hazard is confirmed harder than filed: 0/270 calls carry usage in both trees. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-hermes-trace-usage-provenance-design.md §2.4.

TB-18 Tasks 3-6 validation, live corpus (not fixtures).

Exported a fresh trace corpus via `hermes sessions export --format trace --newer-than 30d` (784 sessions -- larger than Task 2's 64-file check, since more sessions now exist). Ran the full pipeline against all 784 files:

- 784/784 files claimed by HermesTraceParser (0 by ClaudeParser, 0 AmbiguousSchema)
- 2233/2233 tool calls stamped usage_provenance=ABSENT_BY_EXPORT (0 fabricated PRESENT/other)
- passive.py Tool Leaderboard: 32 rows render n/a or n/a*; 0 rows render "no" (the pre-fix bug: a corpus with no usage channel reporting a measured zero it never measured)
- probe.py: 784/784 files refused at dispatch with NonIsolableTurns ("hermes --format trace carries no requestId ... (S30)")

Full gate: ruff clean; mypy --strict at the 38-error baseline (0 new); pytest 247 passed, 1 skipped, 3 subtests passed.

Own-reviewer code review: PASS, no Critical/Major findings (attached separately, role=review). Tasks 3-6 complete on branch chore/add-hermes-cli-export-plan, PR #20.

TB-18 Tasks 3-6 complete. Bumped in_progress -> review.

SHIPPED (this run, on top of Tasks 0-2 already landed):
- Task 3: passive.py usage_missing counter + four-case cache_note render (yes/no/n/a/n/a*)
- Task 4: 5 probe fixtures migrated to carry requestId, grouping unchanged (45 passed before/after)
- Task 5: probe.py refuses non-isolable turns -- NonIsolableTurns, no ts: fallback, dispatch-level trace refusal
- Task 6: SPEC.md S29/S30 confirmed already landed (Phase 0 intake, no-op this task); README status refreshed; ticket token-claim correction posted

PR #20 (chore/add-hermes-cli-export-plan): pushed, body rewritten to describe Tasks 0-6, TB-19 shared-file overlap named. head=5c74901, base=28b6187, mergeable=MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus=CLEAN.

TEST COUNTS: 232 passed/1 skipped (Task 2 close) -> 247 passed/1 skipped/3 subtests (final). ruff clean throughout. mypy --strict held at the 38-error baseline, 0 new, every commit.

OWN-REVIEW: PASS, no Critical/Major findings.

VALIDATION: live corpus, not fixtures -- 784 freshly-exported hermes trace sessions, 784/784 -> HermesTraceParser, 2233/2233 calls ABSENT_BY_EXPORT, 0 tool-leaderboard rows render "no" (the bug), probe refuses all 784/784.

DEVIATIONS (flagged inline, per hard rules):
1. render_report() gained 5 required kwargs after the plan was drafted -- Task 3's test helper updated to pass them (RED commit 5d20a2f).
2. SPEC.md S29/S30 already present from Phase 0 intake (305d7d8) -- Task 6 Step 1 was a no-op; amendment block added to the plan file (commit 4cfd5d1) documenting this before implementation began.
3. Test-count baseline drifted from the plan's stated cumulative figures (hermetic-suite fix, 5baeca1, predates this plan) -- actual gate counts reported at each step instead.

No architectural drift. Stopping here -- orchestrator owns everything past review.
